pyramids-of-giza.fact: Khufu's pyramid was the tallest building on Earth for about 3,800 years. Its sides line up almost exactly with north.

saqqara.fact: Imhotep stacked six stone platforms for King Djoser and invented the pyramid. Later pyramids here carry the oldest religious texts known.

karnak-temple.fact: Around thirty pharaohs added to it. It was the home of Amun, king of the gods, and the richest temple in Egypt.

luxor-temple.fact: Begun by Amenhotep III, finished by Ramesses II. A Roman chapel and a working mosque stand inside its walls.

valley-of-the-kings.fact: Over sixty tombs are known. Tutankhamun's was found almost intact in 1922 after 3,200 years.

temple-of-hatshepsut.fact: Built for a woman who ruled as pharaoh for some twenty years. Her successor tried to erase her name.

abu-simbel.fact: Twice a year the rising sun reaches the statues deep inside. The whole hill was cut up and raised 65 m in the 1960s.

philae.fact: One of the last places where the old gods were worshipped. The final dated hieroglyphs were carved here in AD 394.

temple-of-edfu.fact: Dedicated to Horus and buried in sand for centuries, which is why it survives so completely.

dendera.fact: Temple of Hathor, goddess of love and music. Cleopatra is carved on its back wall.

siwa-oasis.fact: Its oracle told Alexander he was the son of a god. People here still speak Siwi, a Berber language.

saint-catherine-s-monastery.fact: Built where tradition places the burning bush. Its library of ancient manuscripts is second only to the Vatican's.

petra.when: mostly 1st century BC to 1st century AD
petra.fact: Arab traders who grew rich on incense and became masters of desert water. The Treasury is 39 m of solid carved cliff.

jerash.fact: One of ten allied cities called the Decapolis. Its colonnaded street still shows chariot ruts.

wadi-rum.fact: Around 25,000 rock carvings and 20,000 inscriptions record 12,000 years of people passing through.

hegra-madain-salih.fact: Over a hundred carved tombs. Many carry the date, the owner's name and even the mason's signature.

baalbek.fact: Its foundation stones weigh around 800 tons each. How they were moved is still debated.

byblos.fact: It traded papyrus to the Greeks, who named books, and so the Bible, after it.

palmyra.fact: Queen Zenobia led it in revolt and briefly took Egypt from Rome.

old-city-of-jerusalem.fact: The Dome of the Rock (AD 691) stands on the site of the Jewish Temple, minutes from the Holy Sepulchre.

masada.fact: Jewish rebels held out here against Rome until AD 73 or 74. The siege ramp is still there.

gobekli-tepe.fact: Seven thousand years older than the pyramids, before pottery, metal or writing. It overturned the idea that farming came before temples.

mount-nemrut.fact: King Antiochus mixed Greek and Persian gods and seated himself among them. His tomb has never been found.

ani.fact: At its height it rivalled Constantinople. It was abandoned after Mongols, earthquakes and moved trade routes.

sumela-monastery.fact: Monks lived on this ledge, around 300 m above the valley floor, until 1923.

istanbul-hagia-sophia.fact: Built in under six years. Its dome was the largest enclosed space in the world for nearly a thousand years.

ephesus.fact: Home of the Temple of Artemis, one of the Seven Wonders. The sea has since moved several kilometres away.

cappadocia.fact: Underground towns such as Derinkuyu go down eighteen levels and could shelter thousands.

hattusa.fact: A superpower that fought Ramesses II and then signed one of the oldest surviving peace treaties.

pamukkale-hierapolis.fact: Romans came for the hot water. A cave here breathed deadly gas and was called the gate to the underworld.

acropolis-of-athens.fact: The Parthenon's lines are very slightly curved so that they look straight. It has been temple, church and mosque.

delphi.fact: Kings asked the Pythia before going to war. "Know thyself" was carved at the entrance.

meteora.fact: Monks first went up by rope and net. Six of twenty-four monasteries are still lived in.

mycenae.fact: The warriors of Homer's Troy stories. Gold death masks were found in its royal graves.

olympia.fact: Wars paused for the games for over a thousand years. The Olympic flame is still lit here.

knossos.fact: Europe's first great civilisation, with bull-leaping, running water and a script nobody can read.

delos.fact: So sacred that nobody was allowed to be born or die here. Later a huge, tax-free Roman port.

santorini-akrotiri.fact: Three-storey houses with fresh wall paintings, sealed by one of the largest eruptions in human history.

ancient-rome.fact: The Pantheon is still the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world after 1,900 years.

pompeii.fact: Bakeries with bread, election slogans and bodies caught in ash. A third is still unexcavated.

paestum.fact: Three temples better preserved than most in Greece, and a rare painted tomb of a diver.

valley-of-the-temples.fact: Akragas was one of the richest Greek cities. The Temple of Concordia survived by becoming a church.

segesta.fact: Built by a people who claimed to descend from Troy, and left without a roof. Nobody knows why.

hypogeum-maltese-temples.fact: An underground sanctuary carved with antler and stone. One chamber makes a deep voice echo through the whole complex.

ggantija.fact: Older than Stonehenge and the pyramids. Locals believed giants had built it.

su-nuraxi-nuraghe.fact: A tower of dry stone in a ruined village. Sardinia has some 7,000 such towers and no written records of who built them.

split-diocletian-s-palace.fact: Built for the only Roman emperor who retired, to grow cabbages. About 3,000 people live inside its walls.

mostar.fact: The single arch stood 427 years until it was destroyed in 1993. It was rebuilt with the same stone.

bay-of-kotor.fact: Not a real fjord but a drowned river canyon. Kotor's walls climb 260 m up the mountain.

butrint.fact: Virgil says Trojan refugees founded it. A baptistery floor shows a whole paradise in mosaic.

rila-monastery.fact: Founded by a hermit who lived in a cave nearby. It kept the Bulgarian language alive under Ottoman rule.

alhambra.fact: The last Muslim palace of Spain. Its walls carry around 10,000 inscriptions, many of them poems.

mosquecathedral-of-cordoba.fact: Over 850 columns, many reused from Roman buildings. Córdoba was then one of the largest cities in Europe.

barcelona-sagrada-familia.fact: Gaudí knew he would never see it finished. "My client is not in a hurry," he said of God.

santiago-the-camino.fact: Pilgrims have walked here for over a thousand years to the tomb said to be of Saint James.

altamira.fact: When it was found in 1879 experts called it fake, because they thought early people could not paint so well.

tomar-templar-convent.fact: When the Templars were banned, Portugal simply renamed them. They later financed the voyages of discovery.

sintra.fact: The Quinta da Regaleira has a spiral well used for secret initiations, never for water.

lascaux-the-dordogne.fact: Found by four teenagers in 1940. Nearly 2,000 figures, some animals over five metres long.

carnac-stones.fact: Rows of stones run for kilometres. Legend says they are a Roman army turned to stone.

mont-saint-michel.fact: The tide can rise 14 m. The abbey was never taken in the Hundred Years' War.

chartres-cathedral.fact: Most of its original windows survive, in a blue glassmakers have struggled to copy.

provence-pont-du-gard.fact: The aqueduct drops only about 12 m in 50 km. It was built without mortar on its arches.

stonehenge-avebury.fact: The smaller bluestones were brought over 200 km from Wales. Its axis follows the solstice sun.

orkney-skara-brae.fact: Stone beds, dressers and indoor drains, hidden under a dune until a storm in 1850.

callanish-stones.fact: Every 18.6 years the moon seems to roll along the hills and set among the stones.

newgrange.fact: For about 17 minutes at winter solstice, sunrise lights the tomb. It was built 600 years before Giza.

skellig-michael.fact: A dozen monks lived on this rock for centuries, 600 steps above the Atlantic.

norwegian-fjords-stave-churches.fact: Dragons guard the roof beside the crosses. Once there were over a thousand such churches; 28 remain.

iceland.fact: Þingvellir held one of the oldest parliaments in the world, in the rift between two continents.

visby.fact: A merchant city so rich that its fall to the Danes in 1361 became a legend.

krakow-wieliczka.fact: Miners carved chapels, lakes and chandeliers of salt for 700 years, down to 327 m.

prague.fact: The largest ancient castle complex in the world. The astronomical clock has run since 1410.

kyiv.fact: Saint Sophia's mosaics survive almost unchanged from the time of the first Slavic Christian state.

mtskheta-tbilisi.fact: Georgia became Christian around 326. Legend says Christ's robe is buried beneath the cathedral.

gergeti-trinity-church.fact: Built at 2,170 m. In times of danger, the country's treasures were hidden here.

svaneti-ushguli.when: towers from about the 9th to 13th century
svaneti-ushguli.fact: Each family had its own defence tower. Ushguli is among the highest villages in Europe, at around 2,100 m.

geghard-garni.fact: Half of the monastery is carved inside the cliff. Armenia was the first Christian state, around 301.

tatev-monastery.fact: A medieval university above a gorge. It had a swaying pillar said to warn of earthquakes.

persepolis.fact: Delegations of 23 nations are carved bringing gifts. Alexander burned it in 330 BC.

isfahan.fact: "Isfahan is half the world," people said. The square was laid out for polo and is one of the largest on Earth.

ur-babylon.fact: Mesopotamia gave us the first cities, writing and laws. Tradition makes Ur the birthplace of Abraham.

samarkand.fact: Tamerlane's capital. His grandson Ulugh Beg measured the year here to within a minute.

bukhara.fact: Genghis Khan levelled the city but is said to have spared the 46 m minaret because it amazed him.

khiva.fact: An oasis town on the desert road to Persia, known for its slave market and its turquoise towers.

merv.fact: Around 1150 perhaps half a million people lived here. The Mongols destroyed it in 1221.

mogao-caves.fact: 492 painted caves. A sealed library opened in 1900 held some 50,000 documents and the oldest dated printed book.

xi-an-terracotta-army.fact: Guards the first emperor, whose tomb mound is still unopened. Records speak of rivers of mercury inside.

beijing-great-wall.fact: Twenty-four emperors lived in the Forbidden City. All the walls together measure over 21,000 km.

longmen-grottoes.fact: The great Buddha is said to have the face of Empress Wu, the only woman to rule China in her own name.

leshan-giant-buddha.fact: A monk had it carved to calm the rivers. The stone that fell in did make the water safer.

zhangjiajie.fact: Over 3,000 quartz pillars. One was renamed after the film Avatar.

lhasa-potala-palace.fact: A thousand rooms and 13 storeys above Lhasa, winter home of the Dalai Lamas until 1959.

mount-kailash.fact: The home of Shiva. Pilgrims walk 52 km around it; climbing it is forbidden.

kathmandu-valley.fact: Three royal cities in one valley. A young girl is still chosen as the living goddess Kumari.

lumbini.fact: Emperor Ashoka's pillar of 249 BC marks the Buddha's birthplace, with a pond and a sacred tree.

bhutan-tiger-s-nest.fact: Guru Rinpoche is said to have flown here on a tigress. Bhutan measures Gross National Happiness.

agra-taj-mahal.fact: Shah Jahan built it for Mumtaz Mahal. Around 20,000 people worked on it, and it changes colour through the day.

varanasi.fact: One of the oldest living cities on Earth. Hindus believe that dying here frees the soul.

khajuraho.fact: Of 85 temples about 25 survive, saved by the jungle. Only a tenth of the carvings are erotic.

golden-temple-amritsar.fact: Open on four sides to welcome everyone. The free kitchen has never closed.

jaipur-rajasthan.fact: Warrior clans who built hill forts and mirrored halls where one candle lights a whole room.

ellora-ajanta.when: Ajanta from 200 BC, Ellora to AD 1000
ellora-ajanta.fact: The Kailasa temple was cut top-down from one mountain. Some 200,000 tons of rock were removed.

sanchi.fact: Begun by Ashoka, who turned to Buddhism after a terrible war. Early carvings show the Buddha only as a footprint or tree.

hampi.fact: Once the second largest city in the world after Beijing. One temple has pillars that ring like music.

meenakshi-temple-madurai.fact: Every night the god is carried to the goddess's room, and every morning woken with song.

great-living-chola-temples.fact: The capstone weighs around 80 tons and sits 60 m up. The Cholas sailed as far as Sumatra.

mahabalipuram.fact: A port of the sea trade to Asia. The 2004 tsunami uncovered carvings that had been under sand.

konark-sun-temple.fact: The wheels work as sundials. Sailors called it the Black Pagoda and used it to navigate.

sigiriya.fact: A king who murdered his father built his palace up here. The mirror wall has poems left by visitors over 1,000 years ago.

kandy-temple-of-the-tooth.when: tooth kept in Kandy since about 1595
kandy-temple-of-the-tooth.fact: Whoever held the relic had the right to rule. Each summer it parades with a hundred elephants.

anuradhapura.fact: Capital for some 1,300 years. One brick stupa was among the tallest buildings of its age, after the pyramids.

bagan.fact: Over 10,000 temples were built in about 250 years. Some 2,200 remain.

shwedagon-pagoda.when: perhaps 6th to 10th century, legend says older
shwedagon-pagoda.fact: Said to hold eight hairs of the Buddha. Its tip carries thousands of diamonds.

sukhothai.fact: Its name means dawn of happiness. Thai script was created here.

ayutthaya.fact: Around 1700 it was one of the world's largest cities, with Dutch, Japanese and Persian quarters.

chiang-mai-temples.fact: A white elephant carrying a relic climbed the mountain, circled three times and died, so they built here.

white-temple.fact: A private life's work planned to be finished around 2070. Superheroes appear among the murals.

angkor.fact: The largest city of the pre-industrial world, run on canals and reservoirs. It faces west, towards death and Vishnu.

banteay-srei.fact: Built by a scholar, not a king. The carving is so fine that people called it the citadel of women.

preah-vihear-temple.fact: An 800 m causeway climbs to a cliff 525 m above the plain. Two countries took it to court.

wat-phou.fact: A natural stone peak shaped like a Shiva symbol made this mountain holy before Angkor existed.

luang-prabang.civ: Lan Xang, kingdom of a million elephants
luang-prabang.fact: Each dawn hundreds of monks walk silently for rice.

plain-of-jars.fact: Over 2,000 jars up to three metres high, linked to burials. Legend says giants brewed rice wine in them.

my-son.fact: Bricks joined so finely that nobody is sure how. Most of it was bombed in 1969.

hue-imperial-city.fact: A forbidden city modelled on Beijing. Each emperor designed his own tomb as a garden.

ha-long-bay.when: limestone, up to 500 million years in the making
ha-long-bay.fact: Legend says a dragon's tail cut the valleys and its jewels became the islands.

borobudur.fact: A walk up to enlightenment past 2,600 carved panels. It lay under ash and jungle for centuries.

prambanan.fact: Built by Hindu rivals about an hour from Buddhist Borobudur. Legend: a thousand temples in one night.

bali-temples.fact: In 1963 lava from Mount Agung passed within metres of Besakih. The island has tens of thousands of temples.

komodo.fact: The largest lizards alive, up to three metres, with venom. Only around 3,000 are left in the wild.

tana-toraja.when: living tradition, graves some centuries old
tana-toraja.fact: Families keep their dead at home for months or years before a great funeral with buffalo.

raja-ampat.when: reef in the heart of the Coral Triangle
raja-ampat.fact: Around 1,400 kinds of fish and three quarters of all coral species.

batu-caves-kuala-lumpur.fact: Caves 400 million years old. Over a million people come for Thaipusam.

borneo-kinabalu.fact: Older than the Amazon. The mountain is believed to be where souls rest.

banaue-rice-terraces.fact: Carved by hand from the forest down. End to end they would circle half the Earth.

palawan-el-nido.fact: Cliffs of ancient coral and limestone. Tabon Cave holds some of the oldest human remains in the Philippines.

kyoto-temples.fact: Capital for over a thousand years. It was taken off the atomic bomb list in 1945 because of its beauty.

nara-todai-ji.fact: The bronze Buddha weighs about 500 tons. Squeezing through a hole in a pillar is said to bring luck.

miyajima-hiroshima.fact: The whole island was sacred, so commoners had to arrive by boat through the gate.

ise-grand-shrine.fact: Always new and always ancient. The next rebuilding is planned for 2033.

mount-koya.fact: Monks still bring meals twice a day to the founder, who is believed to be meditating since 835.

nikko.fact: The tomb of the first shogun, with the three wise monkeys. One pillar is left wrong on purpose.

gyeongju-bulguksa.fact: Nearby royal mounds held golden crowns. Silla ruled for almost a thousand years.

haeinsa.fact: 81,258 printing blocks with almost no errors, kept dry for centuries by the building's own ventilation.

mongolia-karakorum.fact: Capital of the largest land empire in history. Its stones were reused to build the monastery.

teotihuacan-mexico-city.fact: Home to 100,000 people or more. The Aztecs found it empty and named it the place where gods were made.

monte-alban-oaxaca.fact: One of the first cities in the Americas, with some of its earliest writing.

palenque.fact: King Pakal ruled for 68 years. His tomb, deep in a pyramid, held a mask of jade.

chichen-itza.fact: A clap at the pyramid's foot echoes like the sacred quetzal bird. The steps count 365.

uxmal.fact: The Magician's pyramid has rounded sides. Over 20,000 cut stones cover the Governor's Palace.

calakmul.fact: Tikal's great rival. One pyramid is 45 m high and you may climb above the jungle.

tulum.fact: A walled port for obsidian and jade, seen by the first Spanish ships.

tikal.fact: Laser scans showed tens of thousands of hidden buildings around it. Temple IV rises to about 65 m.

antigua-lake-atitlan.fact: Ruined by the earthquake of 1773. Twelve villages around the lake still speak Maya languages.

caracol.fact: It defeated Tikal in 562. Its pyramid is still among the tallest structures in Belize.

lamanai.fact: Its name means submerged crocodile. People stayed here long after other Maya cities fell.

copan.fact: A stairway of some 2,200 glyphs is the longest known Maya text.

joya-de-ceren.fact: A village left so fast that meals stayed on the table. It shows ordinary Maya life, not kings.

great-blue-hole-reef.fact: A cave that collapsed when seas rose. It is 300 m wide and some 125 m deep.

san-blas-islands.fact: Around 365 islands. The Guna won their autonomy and sew their history into molas.

havana.fact: All the treasure of the Americas gathered here before sailing to Spain.

st-lucia-the-pitons.fact: The island changed hands between France and Britain fourteen times.

antigua-nelson-s-dockyard.fact: Nelson hated his years here. It is the only Georgian dockyard still in use.

lost-city-ciudad-perdida.fact: Reached by about 1,200 stone steps. The Kogi, their descendants, still guard these mountains.

cartagena.fact: Pirates attacked it so often that Spain built 11 km of walls.

san-agustin.fact: The largest group of religious monuments in South America, and we do not know their makers' name.

galapagos-islands.when: islands up to about 4 million years old
galapagos-islands.fact: Finches and tortoises that differ from island to island led Darwin to evolution.

machu-picchu-sacred-valley.fact: A royal estate used for less than a century. The Spanish never found it.

cusco-sacsayhuaman.fact: The navel of the world. Its walls use blocks over 100 tons, fitted without mortar.

nazca-lines.fact: Hundreds of drawings. New ones are still being found with drones and artificial intelligence.

chan-chan.fact: Perhaps 40,000 people lived in this city of mud, until the Inca marched them away.

kuelap.fact: Walls up to 20 m high at 3,000 m. Their round houses were full of carved diamonds.

chavin-de-huantar.fact: Priests used dark tunnels, the roar of water and conch trumpets to overwhelm visitors.

caral.fact: As old as Giza. No weapons or walls were found, but plenty of flutes.

tiwanaku-lake-titicaca.fact: The Inca believed the world began at this lake, at 3,800 m. The Gate of the Sun is one block.

salar-de-uyuni.fact: 10,000 square kilometres of salt, so flat that satellites use it for calibration.

easter-island-rapa-nui.fact: Nearly 1,000 statues. Islanders say they walked, and tests show that they could have.

patagonia.fact: The towers were cut by ice. People have lived here for over 10,000 years.

perito-moreno-glacier.when: part of the third largest ice reserve
perito-moreno-glacier.fact: The front is 5 km wide and 70 m high. Every few years it dams a lake and bursts.

cueva-de-las-manos.fact: Hundreds of stencilled hands, nearly all left ones, sprayed through bone pipes.

iguazu-falls.fact: The Guaraní say a jealous god split the river to stop two lovers fleeing by canoe.

rio-de-janeiro.fact: For 13 years Rio was the capital of the Portuguese Empire, the only time a European empire was ruled from a colony.

serra-da-capivara.when: art up to about 12,000 years old or more
serra-da-capivara.fact: Over 1,000 painted sites. Some finds may push back the date people reached America.

ouro-preto.fact: In its gold rush it was bigger than New York. Aleijadinho carved its churches after losing his fingers.

mesa-verde.fact: Cliff Palace had some 150 rooms. They left within a generation, probably because of drought.

chaco-canyon.fact: Walls follow solstice and moon. Arrow-straight roads lead out across the desert.

grand-canyon-monument-valley.when: up to 1.8 billion years of rock
grand-canyon-monument-valley.fact: The Hopi say their ancestors came into this world through the canyon.

cahokia.fact: Around 1100 it was as big as London. Its main mound covers more ground than the Great Pyramid.

yellowstone.fact: The first national park (1872) sits on a supervolcano with half the world's geysers.

hawaii.fact: They crossed 4,000 km of ocean by stars and swell. Kīlauea is the home of the goddess Pele.

l-anse-aux-meadows.fact: Wood cut here was dated to exactly 1021, almost five centuries before Columbus.

haida-gwaii.fact: Totem poles at SGang Gwaay are left to return to the earth, as tradition asks.

nan-madol.fact: Called the Venice of the Pacific. Some 750,000 tons of basalt were moved, and nobody knows how.

raiatea-marae-taputapuatea.fact: Canoes left from here for Hawaiʻi and New Zealand, carrying a stone to found new temples.

marquesas-islands.fact: Their full-body tattooing was the finest in the Pacific. Gauguin and Jacques Brel are buried here.

bora-bora.fact: Its first name was Pora Pora, first born. The Americans built its airstrip in 1943.

tuamotu-atolls.fact: The largest group of atolls on Earth. Every July thousands of groupers gather in Fakarava's pass.

cook-islands.fact: The great canoes that settled New Zealand are said to have left from Rarotonga.

tonga.fact: The first place in Polynesia to be settled. Its sea empire lasted centuries and its monarchy still reigns.

samoa.fact: Pulemelei is the largest ancient mound in Polynesia. Robert Louis Stevenson is buried above Apia.

fiji.fact: Fire-walkers on Beqa island still cross white-hot stones.

vanuatu-mount-yasur.fact: Mount Yasur has erupted almost without pause for centuries. Over 100 languages are spoken.

new-caledonia.fact: The Lapita culture that settled the Pacific is named after a beach here.

new-zealand-south-island.fact: The last large land people ever reached. Milford Sound was carved by glaciers.

northland-maori-heritage.fact: Where Māori chiefs and the British Crown signed a treaty. The kauri Tāne Mahuta may be 2,000 years old.

uluru.fact: Its caves and marks are the stories of ancestors. Climbing ended in 2019 out of respect.

kakadu.when: art up to 20,000 years old or more
kakadu.fact: People nearby for up to 65,000 years: the oldest living culture on Earth.

great-barrier-reef.fact: 2,300 km long. Aboriginal stories remember the time when the sea rose over the land.

tasmania.fact: A prison where some were kept in total silence, amid some of the cleanest air in the world.

rock-churches-of-lalibela.fact: A new Jerusalem carved downwards from the rock. Legend says angels worked the night shift.

aksum.fact: One of the great powers of its age beside Rome and Persia. The tallest obelisk was 33 m, a single stone.

pyramids-of-meroe.fact: Sudan has more pyramids than Egypt. Warrior queens called Kandakes fought Rome.

leptis-magna.fact: Home town of Emperor Septimius Severus, who rebuilt it in marble.

el-jem-carthage.fact: It held 35,000 people. Carthage, Hannibal's city, was burned by Rome in 146 BC.

kairouan.fact: The mosque's minaret is one of the oldest in the world. Its prayer hall reuses Roman columns.

timgad-djemila.fact: A town for retired soldiers. A stone game board there reads: hunt, bathe, play, laugh, that is life.

volubilis-fes.fact: Fes has the oldest continuously running university, founded in 859, by tradition by a woman.

ait-benhaddou-the-desert.fact: A caravan stop between Timbuktu and Marrakesh. It has been Jerusalem and Egypt in many films.

djenne.fact: Every year the whole town replasters the mosque by hand in one day.

abomey-ouidah.fact: A kingdom with an army of women. Vodun began here and crossed the ocean with the enslaved.

goree-dakar.fact: The House of Slaves and its door of no return became a symbol for millions.

great-zimbabwe.fact: Colonists refused to believe that Africans had built it. Chinese porcelain was found inside.

victoria-falls.fact: 1.7 km wide and 108 m high. At full moon the spray makes a rainbow at night.

okavango-delta.when: a river that never reaches the sea
okavango-delta.fact: The San have lived here for tens of thousands of years. The flood arrives in the dry season.

namib-dunes.when: desert at least 55 million years old
namib-dunes.fact: Perhaps the oldest desert on Earth. The dead trees of Deadvlei have stood for some 600 years.

cape-town-the-cape.when: mountain of rock some 450 million years old
cape-town-the-cape.fact: Robben Island held Nelson Mandela for 18 years. Sailors called it the Cape of Storms.

kilwa-kisiwani.fact: It controlled the gold of Great Zimbabwe and minted its own coins.

zanzibar.fact: The sultan of Oman moved his capital here for the cloves.

serengeti.fact: Olduvai Gorge and Laetoli show our earliest ancestors. Over a million wildebeest walk past.

lamu.fact: The oldest Swahili town still lived in, with more donkeys than cars.

mountain-gorillas-bwindi.fact: About half of the 1,000 or so mountain gorillas left on Earth live here.

tsingy-of-madagascar.fact: Tsingy means where one cannot walk barefoot. Most species here live nowhere else.

avenue-of-the-baobabs.when: trees up to 800 years old or more
avenue-of-the-baobabs.fact: Called mothers of the forest. They are the last of a dense forest that once stood here.

mauritius.fact: Home of the dodo, gone by 1681. Le Morne's cliffs sheltered people escaping slavery.

reunion.fact: One of the most active volcanoes in the world. The inner valleys were settled by escaped slaves.

seychelles.fact: Pieces of a lost continent, with the largest seed of any plant, the coco de mer.

maldives.fact: Buddhist for over a thousand years until 1153. The islands lie on average 1.5 m above the sea.

socotra.fact: A third of its plants grow nowhere else. Their red resin was sold to Rome as dragon's blood.

oman-nizwa-the-desert.fact: Its tower has traps for boiling date syrup. Water channels from about AD 500 still run.

saint-helena.fact: Napoleon died here in 1821. Its tortoise Jonathan, hatched about 1832, is the oldest land animal ever recorded.

azores.when: islands up to 8 million years old
azores.fact: Pico, 2,351 m, is the highest mountain of Portugal. Whaling lookouts now guide whale watchers.

canary-islands.fact: The Guanche mummified their dead and whistled a language across the valleys.

madeira.fact: Over 2,000 km of hand-cut channels carry water across the island.

cape-verde.fact: The first European town in the tropics. Morna, the music of longing, was born here.

svalbard.fact: The Global Seed Vault here keeps over a million crop samples safe in permafrost.

antarctica.when: ice up to 34 million years old
antarctica.fact: It holds about 60 percent of the planet's fresh water and belongs to no one.

karahan-tepe.fact: More than 250 T-shaped pillars lie here, and people seem to have lived beside their temple.

catalhoyuk.fact: Up to 8,000 people lived here, with the dead buried under their beds and bulls' heads on the walls.

askl-hoyuk.fact: Here people slowly learned to keep sheep. One of the earliest known skull operations was done here.

ancient-jericho.fact: A stone tower of 8000 BC still stands 8 m high, older than any wall of its kind.

choirokoitia.fact: They sailed here with their animals and lived in stone beehive houses.

agar-qim-mnajdra.fact: At the equinox the sun shines straight through Mnajdra's doorway. One stone weighs over 20 tons.

tarxien-temples.fact: Stone rollers found here show how the blocks were moved.

antequera-dolmens.fact: Its roof stone weighs some 150 tons, more than any stone at Stonehenge.

los-millares.fact: Forts, aqueduct and 80 tombs, from a culture that vanished.

almendres-cromlech.fact: About 95 egg-shaped stones among cork oaks, one of the oldest stone circles in Europe.

coa-valley-rock-art.fact: A dam was stopped to save these thousands of engravings.

el-castillo-cave.fact: Among the oldest dated cave paintings on Earth. You see the originals.

atapuerca.fact: In the Pit of Bones lay 28 people 430,000 years old, the ancestors of Neanderthals.

chauvet-cave.fact: Twice as old as Lascaux and just as good. You visit a perfect replica in the Ardèche.

pech-merle.fact: A child's footprints are preserved in the clay. You see original paintings.

font-de-gaume.fact: Over 200 animals. Very few visitors are allowed each day.

niaux-cave.fact: The drawings look as if they were made yesterday.

rouffignac-cave-of-a-hundred-mammoths.fact: 158 mammoths, beside the scratch marks of cave bears.

gavrinis.fact: Every wall swirls with carvings. Its roof stone is part of a broken giant menhir 4 km away.

cairn-of-barnenez.fact: Eleven chambers under 12,000 tons of stone, two thousand years before the pyramids.

filitosa.fact: The carved warriors may show the Sea Peoples who shook the ancient world.

valcamonica-rock-art.fact: One of the largest collections on Earth, in use for 8,000 years.

giants-tombs-of-sardinia.fact: Coddu Vecchiu's stele is 4 m high. People still lie on the stones to be healed.

monte-d-accoddi.fact: It looks like a ziggurat, built before the ziggurats.

otzi-the-iceman-bolzano.fact: He had 61 tattoos, a copper axe and an arrow in his back.

lepenski-vir.fact: Houses shaped like the mountain opposite. Some of the oldest large sculptures in Europe.

varna-the-oldest-gold.fact: One man was buried with more gold than existed in the rest of the world at the time.

perperikon.fact: Thought to be the lost oracle of Dionysus that Alexander's family consulted.

swabian-jura-caves.fact: The Lion-man and the Venus of Hohle Fels come from here, with bone flutes 40,000 years old.

nebra-sky-disc-goseck-circle.fact: Goseck's gates line up with the winter sun and it is 2,000 years older than Stonehenge.

neanderthal-museum.fact: Found by quarry workers in 1856, three years before Darwin's book.

lake-constance-pile-dwellings.fact: Mud preserved their bread, cloth and dugout boats.

heuneburg.fact: Perhaps the city Herodotus called Pyrene, the oldest north of the Alps.

hallstatt.fact: It named a whole age. A Bronze Age wooden staircase was found intact in the mine.

ring-of-brodgar-maeshowe.fact: At midwinter the sunset enters Maeshowe, where Vikings later scratched graffiti.

kilmartin-glen.fact: Over 350 monuments. At Dunadd kings put their foot into a carved print.

bryn-celli-ddu.fact: It was built over an older stone circle that someone had smashed.

grime-s-graves.fact: Over 400 shafts, up to 14 m deep.

knowth-dowth.fact: One stone may be the oldest known map of the moon.

carrowmore.fact: DNA shows the builders' families came from Anatolia.

poulnabrone-the-burren.fact: Thirty-three people lay inside, with axes and beads.

tanum-rock-carvings.fact: The rocks stood at the shore then, and the ships may carry the sun.

alta-rock-carvings.fact: Over 6,000 figures, climbing higher as the land rose from the sea.

ale-s-stones.fact: Its ends point to midsummer sunset and midwinter sunrise.

sarmizegetusa-regia.fact: The lost capital that Trajan conquered, with an andesite sun.

cradle-of-humankind.fact: Homo naledi was found in 2013 through a gap 20 cm wide.

olduvai-gorge-laetoli.fact: At Laetoli three beings walked through wet ash side by side, 3.7 million years ago.

koobi-fora-lake-turkana.fact: Turkana Boy, the most complete early skeleton, was found across the lake.

kondoa-rock-paintings.fact: Healers still leave offerings under the paintings.

tsodilo-hills.fact: The San say the first people were created here.

drakensberg-rock-art.fact: Shamans painted their trance journeys until the 1800s.

twyfelfontein.fact: Seals and penguins are drawn 100 km from the sea.

blombos-pinnacle-point-caves.fact: The oldest known drawing, a red hashtag, comes from Blombos. You can visit Pinnacle Point.

border-cave.fact: Grass beds 200,000 years old and a notched counting bone.

jebel-irhoud.fact: It pushed our species back by 100,000 years in 2017.

tassili-n-ajjer.fact: Crocodiles, cattle and floating round-headed gods, in a forest of stone.

tadrart-acacus.fact: Elephants and giraffes turn slowly into horses and camels.

cave-of-swimmers-gilf-kebir.fact: The film The English Patient made it famous.

ennedi.fact: In Guelta d'Archei crocodiles survive from the green Sahara.

hadar-where-lucy-was-found.fact: Named after the Beatles song playing in camp that night.

tiya-stelae.fact: Nobody knows what the symbols mean.

senegambian-stone-circles.fact: More stone circles than anywhere else on Earth.

msoura-stone-circle.fact: Legend makes it the tomb of the giant Antaeus.

hyrax-hill-kariandusi.when: axes up to 1 million years old
hyrax-hill-kariandusi.fact: Hundreds of hand axes lie where they were dropped.

bhimbetka.fact: Dancers, hunters and tigers in over 700 shelters.

dholavira.fact: It had giant reservoirs and perhaps the world's first signboard, still unread.

lothal.fact: Its bead makers sold to Mesopotamia.

mohenjo-daro.fact: Toilets and drains in every house, and no palace or king.

harappa.fact: Railway builders used its bricks before anyone knew what it was.

gunung-padang.fact: Claims that it is 25,000 years old made it famous. Most archaeologists disagree.

sangiran.fact: People lived here for over a million years.

liang-bua-cave-of-the-hobbit.fact: Found in 2003, hunting dwarf elephants and giant storks.

maros-caves-sulawesi.fact: A scene of people and a pig here is the oldest known story in pictures.

niah-caves.fact: The Deep Skull, painted death ships and swift nest collectors.

ban-chiang.fact: A student tripped over a pot in 1966 and found a lost culture.

zhoukoudian-peking-man.fact: The original bones vanished in 1941 and were never found.

liangzhu-jade-city.fact: China's first known state, and its earliest large water works.

sanxingdui.fact: Found in burned, buried pits, like nothing else in China.

yinxu-shang-capital.fact: The first Chinese writing was found here, sold as dragon bones in pharmacies.

shimao.fact: Jade is set into its walls and skulls lie under its gate.

korean-dolmens.fact: Gochang alone has over 440 in one valley.

sannai-maruyama-jomon-village.fact: The Jōmon made pottery 16,000 years ago, long before farming.

yoshinogari.fact: It may belong to the world of the shaman queen Himiko.

mozu-kofun-tombs.fact: Larger in area than the Great Pyramid, and nobody may enter.

denisova-cave.fact: A girl here had a Neanderthal mother and a Denisovan father.

arkaim.fact: The oldest chariots known come from its people.

tanbaly-petroglyphs.fact: Around 5,000 figures, with rays for heads.

gobustan.fact: Reed boats and dancers. A stone here rings like a tambourine.

zorats-karer-carahunge.fact: Over 80 stones have eyes drilled through them, perhaps for stars.

dmanisi.fact: One old man had lost all his teeth, so others must have fed him.

areni-caves.fact: People trod grapes here 6,000 years ago beside a burial.

shanidar-cave.fact: One man lived long with a crushed arm and a blind eye, helped by his group.

mount-carmel-caves.fact: Nearby Misliya held the oldest Homo sapiens outside Africa.

jubbah-hail-rock-art.fact: Perhaps the oldest pictures of dogs on leads. There was once a lake here.

dilmun-bahrain.fact: Once over 100,000 burial mounds. Gilgamesh came here seeking eternal life.

bat-al-ayn-beehive-tombs.fact: From the copper land that traded with Sumer.

takht-e-soleyman.fact: Persian kings walked here on foot after their coronation.

chogha-zanbil.fact: Thousands of bricks repeat the king's name and a curse on thieves.

shahr-e-sukhteh.fact: A woman here wore an artificial eye, the oldest known.

monte-verde.fact: A bog kept tent pegs, meat and even a child's footprint.

chinchorro-mummies-arica.fact: They mummified everyone, two thousand years before Egypt.

sechin.fact: Its walls show people cut in pieces, and nobody knows why.

poverty-point.fact: They moved two million cubic metres of soil with baskets.

serpent-mound.fact: It lies on the rim of an ancient meteor crater.

head-smashed-in-buffalo-jump.fact: The bones below are 11 m deep.

baja-giant-cave-murals.fact: Some figures are 4 m tall. The Cochimí said giants painted them.

horseshoe-canyon-great-gallery.fact: The Holy Ghost panel is the masterpiece of American rock art.

la-lindosa-rock-art.fact: It may show mastodons and giant sloths, now extinct.

la-venta-olmec-heads.fact: The heads weigh up to 50 tons and came from 100 km away.

stone-spheres-of-costa-rica.fact: Banana companies found hundreds. Their purpose is unknown.

murujuga-rock-art.fact: The Tasmanian tiger and the first known human faces are drawn here.

lake-mungo.fact: Mungo Man and Mungo Lady. Footprints of a running hunter were found nearby.

budj-bim-eel-traps.fact: One of the oldest fish farms in the world, still used.

kuk-swamp.fact: Bananas and taro were first grown here.

troy.fact: Schliemann dug straight through Homer's layer looking for it.

aphrodisias.fact: Its marble school carved statues for all the empire.

pergamon.fact: Parchment is named after it: its library rivalled Alexandria.

didyma-miletus-priene.fact: Builders' drawings are still scratched on the walls.

termessos.fact: Its theatre hangs at 1,000 m among wild forest.

sagalassos.fact: Water flows over nine kinds of marble as it did 1,800 years ago.

lycian-tombs-xanthos-myra-letoon.fact: Twice the people burned their own city rather than surrender.

lake-van-akdamar.fact: The kings of Urartu fought Assyria from here.

gaziantep-zeugma-mosaics.fact: Gaziantep is also Turkey's food capital.

mardin.when: lived in for thousands of years
mardin.fact: In nearby monasteries people still pray in Aramaic, the language of Jesus.

epidaurus.fact: Healing god Asclepius cured people in their dreams here.

mystras.fact: The last emperor of Constantinople was crowned here.

vergina-tomb-of-philip-ii.fact: The tombs were found unrobbed in 1977.

dodona.fact: Questions on lead strips survive, such as: is the child mine?

phaistos.fact: The Phaistos Disc was stamped with movable signs.

samothrace.fact: The Winged Victory of the Louvre stood here.

paphos.fact: The Tombs of the Kings are whole houses cut in rock.

salamis.fact: Legend says a hero of Troy founded it.

herculaneum.fact: A library of burnt scrolls is now being read with artificial intelligence.

hadrian-s-villa-tivoli.fact: Larger than Pompeii, with an island to be alone on.

tarquinia-cerveteri.fact: Husbands and wives dine together for ever, which shocked the Greeks.

matera.fact: In 1950 families still lived in caves with their animals.

selinunte.fact: One temple would have been among the largest ever, but was never finished.

piazza-armerina-mosaics.fact: 3,500 square metres of floor saved by a landslide.

pula.fact: The only one with four side towers left.

lake-ohrid.when: lake over a million years old
lake-ohrid.fact: The Cyrillic alphabet was shaped here.

merida.fact: Its theatre is still used 2,000 years later.

ronda-white-villages.fact: Pileta cave nearby has real Ice Age paintings.

conimbriga.fact: Only a sixth has been dug out.

trier.fact: Emperor Constantine ruled the west from here.

saalburg.fact: The Limes ran 550 km across Germany.

hadrian-s-wall.fact: Vindolanda kept soldiers' letters, including a birthday invitation.

sutton-hoo.fact: Found by a self-taught digger in 1939.

bath.fact: People threw in lead curses against thieves.

jelling.fact: Harald Bluetooth raised one, and gave his name to the radio link.

dougga.fact: A tomb with two languages let us read Libyan.

cyrene.fact: It grew rich on silphium, a plant now extinct.

sabratha.fact: Once a port for wild animals and ivory.

abydos.fact: Its list of kings helped decode Egyptian history. The first pharaohs lie here.

dahshur.fact: Here Sneferu learned how to build a true pyramid.

amarna.fact: Akhenaten and Nefertiti built it in a few years. It was abandoned after him.

medinet-habu.fact: It shows the battle against the Sea Peoples.

kom-ombo.fact: Three hundred crocodile mummies were found here.

alexandria.fact: The lighthouse lies in blocks under the harbour, where you can dive.

kerma.fact: One king was buried with 400 people.

jebel-barkal.fact: From here black pharaohs marched north and ruled Egypt.

loropeni-ruins.fact: The best kept of a hundred forts.

mapungubwe.fact: Its kings traded gold for Chinese pottery.

gedi.fact: Ming vases were found, and nobody knows why people left.

desert-castles-of-jordan.fact: Its dome holds the oldest round map of the sky.

kerak-castle.fact: Saladin spared one tower because a wedding was going on.

little-petra.fact: Beidha nearby is one of the oldest villages you can walk through.

dead-sea-bethany.fact: The shore is 430 m below sea level and sinks a metre a year.

tyre.fact: Alexander built a causeway to take the island city.

krak-des-chevaliers.fact: Two thousand men could live here for five years.

ctesiphon-arch.fact: 37 m high, with no support while it was built.

nineveh.fact: The Epic of Gilgamesh was found here on clay.

hatra.fact: Its temples mix Greek columns and Arab gods.

uruk.fact: King Gilgamesh ruled here. The first texts are lists of beer and sheep.

eridu.fact: Eighteen temples stood on top of each other.

pasargadae.fact: Alexander had it repaired out of respect.

naqsh-e-rostam.fact: Below them a Roman emperor kneels to a Persian.

bam-citadel.fact: Scorpions and palms around an earthen castle.

bamiyan.fact: Oil paint was used here 500 years before Europe.

takht-i-bahi.fact: Here the Buddha was first shown as a Greek-looking man.

taxila.fact: Alexander rested here, and students came for 700 years.

panjakent-sarazm.fact: Sarazm was smelting copper 5,500 years ago.

nalanda.fact: Its library is said to have burned for three months.

bodh-gaya.fact: A descendant of the tree still grows there.

badami-aihole-pattadakal.fact: North and south temple styles stand side by side.

rani-ki-vav-stepwell.fact: A queen built it for her king. Silt hid 500 sculptures.

modhera-sun-temple.fact: At the equinox the sun lit the inner statue.

mumbai-elephanta.fact: One of the great sculptures of the world.

halebidu-belur.fact: No two of its thousands of figures are alike.

ranakpur-dilwara.fact: Dilwara's ceilings are so thin that light shines through.

dambulla.fact: A king hid here and gilded it when he won back his throne.

polonnaruwa.fact: Its king's reservoir is as big as a sea.

mrauk-u.fact: A trading kingdom with samurai guards.

sambor-prei-kuk.fact: The oldest Khmer capital you can visit.

beng-mealea.fact: A mirror of Angkor Wat, never restored.

banteay-chhmar.fact: You can sleep in village homes around it.

phanom-rung-phimai.fact: Four times a year the sun shines through all fifteen doors.

trowulan-majapahit.fact: It claimed all the islands of today's Indonesia.

candi-sukuh-ceto.fact: Frank carvings of giants and turtles in tea hills.

yungang-the-hanging-temple.fact: The faces are said to be those of emperors.

dazu-rock-carvings.fact: Buddhism, Taoism and Confucius share the cliffs.

maijishan-grottoes.fact: 7,200 clay figures hang on a red rock.

guge-kingdom.fact: A rock full of tunnels and perfect murals at 3,700 m.

samye-monastery.fact: Each building stands for a continent.

horyu-ji.fact: Its pagoda has survived every earthquake for 1,300 years.

izumo.fact: Its hall once stood 48 m high on giant pillars.

himeji-castle.fact: The paths inside are a maze made to confuse attackers.

yaxchilan-bonampak.fact: Bonampak's paintings proved that the Maya waged cruel wars.

coba-ek-balam.fact: One Maya road runs 100 km straight.

edzna.fact: The sun lights its rain god's face twice a year.

el-tajin.fact: The flying men still spin down a pole here.

xochicalco.fact: A beam of sun falls through a chimney for 105 days a year.

mitla.fact: The gate to the land of the dead.

cholula-puebla.fact: By volume almost twice the Great Pyramid.

paquime.fact: T-shaped doors tie it to Chaco far to the north.

el-mirador.fact: La Danta is about 72 m high, built before Christ.

yaxha.fact: Five hundred buildings between two lakes.

quirigua.fact: Stela E is 10 m. One date points back 400 million years.

guayabo.fact: Ten thousand people lived here and left before the Spanish.

ollantaytambo.fact: Six 50-ton pink stones were left unfinished. People still live in Inca houses.

choquequirao.fact: White stone llamas climb its terraces.

moray-maras.fact: Perhaps a garden laboratory: each ring has its own climate.

sillustani.fact: They stand at 3,900 m above a silent lake.

lima-pachacamac.fact: Pilgrims fasted for a year to ask the god.

huacas-of-the-sun-and-moon.fact: 140 million bricks, each stamped by its makers.

lord-of-sipan.fact: Police saved it from tomb robbers in 1987.

karajia-revash-cloud-people-tombs.fact: Each figure, 2.5 m tall, holds a mummy.

ingapirca.fact: An oval wall fitted without mortar.

tierradentro-tombs.fact: Up to 7 m underground, with red, black and white walls.

samaipata.fact: A whole hilltop cut into pools, seats and jaguars.

ruins-of-quilmes.fact: The survivors were marched 1,500 km to Buenos Aires.

jesuit-missions-of-paraguay.fact: Guaraní built violins and churches until the order was banned.

canyon-de-chelly.fact: White House ruin sits halfway up a 150 m wall.

bandelier-taos-pueblo.fact: Taos has been lived in without a break for 1,000 years.

lelu-ruins-kosrae.fact: Kings were buried here, then moved to a hole in the reef.

rangiroa.fact: Its lagoon could hold the whole island of Tahiti.

plitvice-lakes.fact: Moss and bacteria build the dams a centimetre a year.

dolomites.fact: They were once a tropical sea floor. Locals call the glow enrosadira.

stromboli-aeolian-islands.fact: Sailors call it the lighthouse of the Mediterranean.

etna.fact: The Greeks put the forge of the gods here. It still grows and shrinks.

giant-s-causeway.fact: A giant is said to have built it to fight another in Scotland.

cliffs-of-moher.fact: Thirty thousand pairs of seabirds nest on them.

lofoten.when: rock up to 3 billion years old
lofoten.fact: The largest Viking house ever found, 83 m, stood here.

vatnajokull-ice-caves.when: ice up to about 1,000 years old
vatnajokull-ice-caves.fact: Seven volcanoes lie beneath the ice.

faroe-islands.fact: A lake seems to hang above the sea. There are more sheep than people.

jokulsarlon-iceland-s-south-coast.fact: It grows every year as the glacier melts.

saxon-bohemian-switzerland.fact: Painters of the Romantic age came here to learn to see.

konigssee-berchtesgaden.when: carved in the last Ice Age
konigssee-berchtesgaden.fact: Boatmen play a trumpet to the echo.

eisriesenwelt-ice-cave.when: cave up to 100 million years old
eisriesenwelt-ice-cave.fact: 42 km long, and lit by hand lamps.

skocjan-postojna-caves.fact: The canyon is 146 m deep. The olm, a blind dragon, lives in the dark.

lake-bled-triglav.fact: Every Slovene is meant to climb Triglav once.

verdon-gorge.fact: Thirty caves here were lived in by early people.

dune-of-pilat.fact: It moves inland up to five metres a year.

chamonix-mont-blanc.fact: First climbed in 1786, the birth of mountaineering.

matterhorn-zermatt.when: a piece of Africa on top of Europe
matterhorn-zermatt.fact: Its peak is African rock pushed over the Alps.

jungfrau-aletsch-glacier.when: shaped by the last Ice Age
jungfrau-aletsch-glacier.fact: 20 km long and shrinking fast. See it soon.

cirque-de-gavarnie.fact: Victor Hugo called it the colosseum of nature.

picos-de-europa.fact: The first peaks sailors saw when coming home from America.

bardenas-reales.fact: Castildetierra looks like a fairy chimney.

timanfaya-lanzarote.fact: Six years of eruption buried a quarter of the island.

la-gomera-its-cloud-forest.fact: People here whistle across valleys, a language taught at school.

samaria-gorge.fact: At the Iron Gates the walls are 4 m apart.

vikos-gorge-zagori.fact: Stone bridges and healers who gathered its herbs.

seven-rila-lakes.fact: White-dressed dancers greet the sun here every August.

danube-delta.fact: Over 300 kinds of birds. Some villages have only boats.

biaowieza-forest.fact: All wild European bison come from a handful saved here and in zoos.

high-tatras.fact: Chamois, bears and a hundred mountain lakes.

white-desert.fact: Shells lie on the sand of a vanished ocean.

ras-mohammed-reefs.when: reef at the tip of Sinai

wadi-mujib-canyon.when: cut to the lowest place on Earth

edge-of-the-world.fact: Corals and shells lie under your feet.

alula-elephant-rock.fact: Thousands of stone rectangles older than the pyramids lie around it.

wahiba-sands-wadi-shab.when: dunes shaped in the Ice Age
wahiba-sands-wadi-shab.fact: Turtles nest on the beach nearby.

musandam-fjords.fact: A village here speaks its own mix of Persian, Arabic and more.

richat-eye-of-the-sahara.when: rock up to 600 million years old
richat-eye-of-the-sahara.fact: Not a crater but a dome worn flat. Some thought it was Atlantis.

ounianga-lakes.fact: Water evaporates and is replaced from deep below.

erg-chebbi-dunes.fact: Pink flamingos come when rain fills its lake.

todra-dades-gorges.fact: Fossils are sold on every corner.

danakil-erta-ale.fact: One of the hottest lived-in places. A new ocean will be born here.

simien-mountains.fact: Geladas are the last grass-eating monkeys.

kilimanjaro.fact: Its glaciers may be gone by about 2050.

ngorongoro-crater.fact: 25,000 large animals live in one bowl.

lake-natron-ol-doinyo-lengai.fact: The lava is as thin as water and turns white. It is the mountain of god.

amboseli.fact: Its elephant families have been studied since 1972.

volcanoes-national-park.fact: Over half of her gorillas' families are still followed.

rwenzori-mountains-of-the-moon.fact: Ptolemy wrote of them 1,900 years ago as the source of the Nile.

murchison-falls.fact: Crocodiles up to five metres wait below.

lake-malawi.fact: Up to a thousand kinds of cichlid, nearly all found only here.

south-luangwa.fact: Leopards by night, carmine bee-eaters by the thousand.

mana-pools.fact: You may walk and canoe among wild animals.

makgadikgadi-salt-pans.fact: One study places the cradle of modern humans here.

etosha.fact: At night black rhinos come to lit waterholes.

fish-river-canyon.fact: A serpent is said to have dug it while fleeing hunters.

skeleton-coast.fact: They called it the land God made in anger.

kruger-blyde-canyon.fact: Larger than Slovenia, with 250 San rock art sites.

isalo.fact: Cliff tombs are opened and turned by families.

andasibe-rainforest.fact: It sounds like a whale in the trees.

everest-base-camp.when: sea floor 470 million years old on top
everest-base-camp.fact: The summit is made of sea creatures. It still rises millimetres a year.

annapurna-mustang.fact: Mustang's cliffs hide thousands of cave rooms 2,000 years old.

chitwan.fact: Rhinos went from under 100 to about 700.

kaziranga.fact: Two thousand rhinos in tall grass.

valley-of-flowers.fact: Over 500 kinds of flowers, found by lost climbers in 1931.

white-rann-of-kutch.fact: Wild asses and flamingo cities. Dholavira lies inside it.

sundarbans.fact: Honey collectors pray to the forest goddess Bonbibi.

kerala-backwaters.fact: Snake boats race with a hundred rowers.

ranthambore-tigers.fact: The fort above is 1,000 years old.

hunza-the-karakoram.fact: They speak a language related to no other.

fann-mountains.fact: One lake is said to hold Alexander's horse.

pamir-highway.fact: Marco Polo rode here past sheep now named after him.

issyk-kul-tian-shan.fact: It never freezes, and drowned towns lie on its bed.

charyn-canyon.fact: A little Grand Canyon with ancient ash trees.

darvaza-door-to-hell.fact: Said to have been lit to burn for a week. The flames are dying down.

lake-baikal.fact: A fifth of the world's fresh water, and seals far from any sea.

kamchatka.fact: The Valley of Geysers was found only in 1941.

gobi-the-flaming-cliffs.fact: A Velociraptor was found here still fighting.

mount-fuji.fact: Sacred for over 1,000 years. It last erupted in 1707.

shiretoko.fact: The name means end of the Earth in Ainu.

yakushima.fact: The forest behind Princess Mononoke. It rains 35 days a month, people say.

jeju.fact: The haenyeo dive for shells without air into their eighties.

taroko-gorge.fact: Parts are closed since the 2024 earthquake, so check first.
